context.brief:
## Employee
- Name: Gandu (no id)
- Role: Instrumentation Engineer, Instrumentation
- Plant / unit: Haldia  / Unit 300

## Equipment history in the knowledge graph
- none found for this profile; interview from the profile alone and ask them to name their key equipment

topics.title: Undocumented daily routines and responsibilities
topics.rationale: Capture tasks performed outside the formal job description that may be critical for continuity.
seed_questions: What tasks did you perform regularly that aren't in your official job description?
Which systems or checks did you monitor informally that no one else knows about?
Are there any daily or weekly routines you developed that your replacement should adopt?

topics.title: Sole-expert instrumentation systems
topics.rationale: Identify single points of failure where only Gandu holds deep knowledge.
seed_questions: Which instruments, loops, or control systems would fail first if you left without a handover?
Are there any custom configurations or settings that only you understand?
What is the most complex system you managed that no one else can troubleshoot?

topics.title: Unfinished or abandoned instrumentation projects
topics.rationale: Surface half-completed work that may pose risks or require immediate attention.
seed_questions: What projects did you start but never complete, and what is their current status?
Are there any modifications you planned or partially implemented that your successor should finish?
Which project, if left unfinished, would cause the most operational risk?

topics.title: Lessons from past project failures
topics.rationale: Avoid repeating mistakes by capturing root causes and vendor/contractor pitfalls.
seed_questions: Can you recall a project that failed or had major issues? What would you do differently?
Which vendors or contractors caused the most problems, and why?
What were the root causes of any instrumentation project delays or cost overruns?

topics.title: Key equipment inventory and criticality
topics.rationale: Since no equipment is recorded, elicit the most important instruments and their undocumented quirks.
seed_questions: What are the top 5 most critical instruments or systems you maintained in Unit 300?
Which equipment gave you the most trouble over the years, and why?
Are there any instruments with known design flaws or installation issues that aren't documented?

topics.title: Undocumented maintenance workarounds
topics.rationale: Capture temporary fixes that became permanent and bypasses not in procedures.
seed_questions: For the equipment you named, are there any 'temporary' fixes that are still in place?
What are the tricks or shortcuts you use to keep critical instruments running?
Are there any manual overrides or bypasses you rely on that aren't in the SOPs?

topics.title: Early warning signs of instrument failure
topics.rationale: Document predictive knowledge like drift patterns, noise, or vibration that precede failures.
seed_questions: What subtle signs indicate an instrument is about to fail, before any alarm triggers?
Are there specific drift trends, noises, or visual cues you've learned to recognize?
How do you distinguish between a false reading and a real process upset on critical loops?

topics.title: Calibration drift and undocumented history
topics.rationale: Capture personal calibration records and deviations from scheduled intervals.
seed_questions: Which instruments tend to drift the most, and how often do you actually calibrate them?
Are there any instruments you calibrate less frequently than scheduled because they're stable?
Do you have personal logs or notes on calibration history that aren't in the CMMS?

topics.title: Unwritten rules and gotchas of Unit 300 instrumentation
topics.rationale: Mandatory tribal topic: surface knowledge that everyone assumes but nobody wrote down.
seed_questions: What are the things nobody wrote down but every instrumentation engineer here should know?
Are there any instruments that are mislabeled, have confusing documentation, or behave unexpectedly?
What is the most dangerous assumption a new engineer might make about this unit's instruments?

topics.title: Vendor and contractor relationship intelligence
topics.rationale: Capture who to call, who to avoid, and informal support channels.
seed_questions: Which vendors have been most reliable for spare parts or emergency support?
Are there any vendor-specific contacts or procedures that aren't in the procurement system?
Who are the go-to people outside the plant when you need urgent instrumentation help?

topics.title: Informal coordination with operations and maintenance
topics.rationale: Document unwritten protocols for cross-department troubleshooting and escalation.
seed_questions: How do you really coordinate with operators when an instrument acts up?
Are there specific operators or mechanics you rely on for informal troubleshooting?
What's the unwritten escalation path when an instrumentation issue becomes critical?

topics.title: Gaps in standard operating procedures
topics.rationale: Identify procedures that are outdated, impractical, or routinely bypassed.
seed_questions: Which procedures do you never follow because they're wrong or impractical?
Are there any calibration or testing steps that are always skipped in practice?
If you could rewrite one procedure, which would it be and what would you change?

topics.title: Tuning parameters and setpoints carried in your head
topics.rationale: Capture critical PID values, alarm limits, and configuration settings not formally recorded.
seed_questions: Are there any PID tuning parameters or alarm setpoints that only you know?
What settings have you tweaked over the years that aren't documented in the DCS or files?
If the control system lost its configuration, what values would you restore from memory first?

topics.title: Future instrumentation needs and obsolescence risks
topics.rationale: Forward-looking advice on upgrades, replacements, and budget priorities.
seed_questions: What upgrades or replacements do you think are urgently needed in the next 5 years?
Are there any obsolete instruments that will be hard to replace or find spares for?
What would you have proposed if you had more budget or management support?

topics.title: Successor advice and open risks
topics.rationale: Mandatory handover topic: critical first-day knowledge and long-term risks.
seed_questions: What are the top three things your replacement needs to know on day one?
What are the biggest risks you see going forward with the instrumentation in Unit 300?
If you could only pass on one piece of wisdom, what would it be?
